title: Sensible heat
objectives: Choose and rearrange Q=mcΔT for a single phase; keep units and signs consistent; separate heat received by water from energy supplied to a whole setup.
difficulty: Beginner through application; final question is a challenge
instructions: Show the equation, substitution, arithmetic and units for numerical answers. Explain physical meaning. Use given constants. Retain intermediate digits and round final answers as requested; for unspecified precision, accept sensible rounding. Graphs and data are simulated educational models.

questions.prompt: What does c represent in Q=mcΔT? Give one consistent unit for c.
A sample warms from 12.0 °C to 29.0 °C. Find ΔT and the sign of Q in the single-phase heating model.
Which requires more heat for the same rise: 50 g or 150 g of the same liquid, with the same c? Give the ratio.
A problem gives m=0.200 kg and c=4.18 J/(g·°C). What mass should be used with that c?
Calculate heat needed to warm 120 g water from 20.0 °C to 35.0 °C. Use c=4.18 J/(g·°C); ignore container effects and losses. Give three significant figures.
A 50.0 g metal sample with c=0.450 J/(g·°C) cools from 80.0 °C to 30.0 °C. Give signed Q and the amount released.
An 80.0 g water sample starts at 18.0 °C and receives 1672 J. Use c=4.18 J/(g·°C). Find final temperature under the single-phase model.

Challenge: A device source supplies 12.0 kJ during an illustrative trial. The 100 g water warms by 8.0 °C, with c=4.18 J/(g·°C). Find the modeled heat gained by the water and the percentage of source energy this represents. Explain why the remainder need not violate conservation.
